and mortals shall no longer reap the splendid ear of corn from the earth;
all things shall remain unsown and unplowed, until mortal men
acknowledge God, the immortal and eternal Ruler of all,
and no longer honor mortal things,
nor glorify dogs and vultures, which Egypt introduced,
with empty mouths and foolish lips.
Only for the pious will the holy land bear all these things:
a stream of honey dripping from rock and spring,
and ambrosial milk shall flow for all the righteous;
for they hoped in one God, the Father, who alone is supreme,
possessing great piety and faith.
But why indeed does my wise mind entrust these things to me?
Now, wretched Asia, I lament piteously for you
and the race of Ionians, Carians, and gold-rich Lydians.
Woe to you, Sardis! Woe, much-beloved Tralles!
Woe, Laodicea, beautiful city! How you shall perish,
destroyed by earthquakes and turned into dust!
In dark Asia [and of the gold-rich Lydians]—
the temple of Artemis at Ephesus, firmly fixed,
shall one day plunge headlong into the divine sea
through chasms and earthquakes, just as storms overwhelm ships.
And Ephesus, prostrate, shall wail, weeping by the shore
and seeking her temple that is inhabited no more.
And then, enraged, the imperishable God dwelling in the ether
shall hurl a hurricane from heaven upon the head of the unholy.
And on that day summer shall take the place of winter.
And then, thereafter, it shall befall mortal men;
for the High Thunderer shall utterly destroy all the shameless
with thunders and lightnings and blazing thunderbolts,
against hostile men, and he shall destroy the impious,
so that the corpses remaining upon the earth will outnumber the sand.
For Smyrna too shall come weeping for her lawgiver
to the gates of Ephesus, and she herself will perish even more.
And foolish Cyme, with her divinely inspired streams,
cast into the hands of godless, unjust, and lawless men,
shall no longer advance her chariot so high into the ether,
but will remain dead among the waters of Cyme.
And then they shall groan aloud together as they await their misery.
The harsh people and shameless tribe of the Cymaeans
shall know the sign they bear in return for the things they suffered.
Then, when they wail over the wretched earth turned to ash,
Lesbos shall be destroyed forever by Eridanus.
Woe to you, Corcyra, beautiful city! Cease your revelry.
And Hierapolis, the only land joined with Pluto,
you shall have the mournful place you longed to have,
buried in the earth beside the streams of Thermodon.
And rocky Tripolis, beside the waters of the Maeander,
allotted to the shore beneath nighttime waves,
this providence of God shall one day utterly destroy you.
lest against my will I seize the neighbor land of Phoebus;
a whirlwind from above will one day destroy luxurious Miletus,
because she chose the deceitful song of Phoebus
and the wise practice and prudent counsel of men.
Be gracious, All-Begetter, to the delicate, fruitful land,
great Judea, that we may behold your purposes.
For this land first you recognized, O God, in favors,
so that it seemed your gracious gift to all mortals
to exist and take heed of what God bestowed.
Thrice-wretched, I long to see the works of the Thracians
and the wall between two seas dragged in the dust by Ares,
swept like a river into the fish-filled deep.
Wretched Hellespont, a child of Assyrians will one day yoke you,
and battle against you will destroy the mighty strength of the Thracians.
An Egyptian king will capture Macedonia,
and a barbarian region will cast down the power of rulers.
Lydians and Galatians, Pamphylians together with Pisidians,
armed in full force, will prevail in evil strife.
Thrice-wretched Italy, you will remain utterly desolate and unwept
in a flourishing land, to perish like a destructive beast.
And the broad sky of the upper air will be above,
a roaring like thunder, to hear the voice of God;
the unquenchable flames of the sun itself will be no more,
nor will the bright light of the moon exist again
in the last time, when God shall reign.
All things will be blackened, and darkness will be over the earth,
and mortals blind, and evil beasts, and misery.
That day will last a long time, so that they perceive
the Lord God himself, all-surveying, high in heaven.
Then he himself will have no pity on hostile men,
who sacrifice herds of lambs and sheep and loud-bellowing bulls
and great calves with gilded horns
to lifeless Hermes-statues and stone gods.
Let divine law, wisdom, and the glory of the righteous lead;
lest the imperishable God, moved to anger, destroy
the whole race of men, livelihood, and the shameless generation;
one must love God the Father, wise and ever-existing.
In the last time, near the end of the moon,
there will be a world-crazed war, stealthy in its deceit.
And a matricidal man will come from the ends of the earth,
a fugitive, meditating sharp designs in his mind,
who will conquer every land and master all things,
and understand all things more prudently than all people;
and that very city for whose sake he himself was ruined, he will seize at once.
He will destroy many men and great tyrants,
and burn them all, as no one else ever did,
and in turn raise up the cowering through zeal.
A great war will come upon mortals from the west,
and blood will flow up to the bank of deep-eddying rivers.
Wrath will drip upon the plains of Macedonia—
and will give an alliance from the west, but destruction to the king.
And then a wintry blast will blow over the earth,
and the plain will again be filled with evil war.
For fire will rain down from heavenly floors upon mortals,
fire and blood, water, thunderbolt, gloom, heavenly night,
and destruction in war, and a mist over the slaughters;
and it will destroy all kings together and noble men.
Then in this way the pitiful destruction of war will cease,
and no longer will anyone fight with swords or with iron,
nor with missiles themselves, which will no longer be lawful.
And the wise people that was left will have peace,
having experienced evil so that they might rejoice hereafter.
Matricides, cease from audacity and wicked daring,
you who of old impurely procured the bed of boys
and set up in brothels prostitutes who were formerly pure,
with outrages, punishment, and laborious shame.
For in you a mother was lawlessly united with her child,
and a daughter was joined as a bride to her own father;
in you also kings defiled their ill-fated mouth;
in you also wicked men found copulation with beasts.
Be silent, utterly mournful, wicked city, keeping revel;
for no longer beside you, with nourishing wood,
will virgin maidens tend the divine fire.
Extinguished by you is the house long longed for,
when for the second time I saw the Temple cast down,
hurled headlong, steeped in fire by an impure hand,
the house ever flourishing, the sanctuary guarding God,
brought forth from the holy ones and being forever imperishable,
hoped for from the soul and body itself.
For not carelessly does it praise God from the unseen earth,
nor did a skilled craftsman make a stone god among them,
nor was golden adornment worshipped, a delusion of souls;
but the great Begetter, God of all divinely inspired beings,
they honored with holy sacrifices and hecatombs.
And now a certain obscure and impure king went up
and threw it down and left it unbuilt,
with a great multitude and illustrious men.
And he himself perished when he set foot upon the land from the immortal earth,
and no longer was such a sign wrought among men
so that others seemed to sack the great city.
For a blessed man came from the heavenly heights,
holding a scepter in his hands, which God gave to him,
and he ruled well over all, and restored to all
the good the wealth which former men had taken.
And every city he took from its foundations with much fire,
and burned the peoples of mortals who previously worked evil;
and the city that God longed for, this he made
brighter than stars and sun and moon,
and he established an adornment, and made a holy . . .
incarnate, fair, and exceedingly beautiful, and fashioned it
a great and boundless tower spanning many stades,
touching the very clouds and visible to all,
so that all the faithful and all the righteous may behold
the glory of the eternal God, the longed-for form;
the east and the west have sung the glory of God.
For no longer are there terrors for wretched mortals,
nor adulteries and unlawful lust with boys,
nor murder nor din of battle, but among all strife is righteous.
This is the final time of the holy ones, when these things are accomplished
by high-thundering God, the founder of the greatest temple.
Alas for you, Babylon, golden-throned, golden-sandaled,
ancient queen holding sway over the world alone,
once great and a city of many people, you will no longer lie
among golden mountains and the streams of the Euphrates;
you will be laid low by the upheaval of an earthquake. And terrible Parthians
made you rule all things. Keep your mouth muzzled, impure
race of the Chaldeans, and neither inquire nor be anxious
how you will rule the Persians or how you will dominate the Medes;
for on account of your rule which you held, sending hostages
to Rome, and those serving as thralls in Asia,
therefore, though thinking yourself queen, you yourself will come into judgment
before adversaries for whose sake you sent ransoms;
and instead of crooked words you will give a bitter reckoning to your enemies.
And in the final time the sea will one day be dry,
and ships will no longer sail to Italy then;
and great Asia will then be all-bearing water,
and Crete a plain. Cyprus will suffer great misery,
and Paphos will bewail a dreadful fate, so that even
Salamis, that great city, will be perceived having suffered great misery;
now again it will be barren dry land upon the shore,
and no few locusts will utterly destroy the Cyprian land.
Looking toward Tyre, you will weep, ill-fated mortals.
Phoenicia, terrible wrath awaits you, until you fall
in a wretched ruin, so that Sirens truly will lament you.
And it will be in the fifth generation, when the destruction of Egypt
will cease, when shameless kings will be mingled together;
and generations of Pamphylians will settle in Egypt,
and in Macedonia and in Asia and among the Lycians
there will be a world-maddening, bloody war in the dust,
which the king of Rome and the rulers of the west will bring to an end.
Whenever the wintry, snowy blast drips
as the great river and the greatest lakes freeze over,
immediately a barbarian horde will march into the land of Asia,
and will destroy the race of terrible Thracians as though powerless.
And then soul-devouring mortals will eat their parents,
consumed by hunger, and will greedily gulp down their food.
And wild beasts will eat the food from the table of every home,
and they themselves and birds will devour all mortals,
and the ocean will be filled with evil from war,
bloody with the flesh and blood of the foolish.
Then there shall be such feebleness over the earth,
that one could discern the number of men and the measure of women.
And a wretched generation shall lament countless times at the end
of the setting sun, so that it may never rise again,
having remained in the waters of Ocean to be submerged;
for it saw the unholy wickednesses of many mortals.
And there will be a moonless gloom around great heaven itself,
and no small mist shall cover the folds of the cosmos
a second time. But thereafter the light of God will guide
the good men, as many as have sung hymns to God.
Isis, thrice-wretched goddess, you shall remain by the waters of the Nile
alone, a speechless maenad upon the sands of Acheron,
and no longer will memory of you remain throughout all the earth.
And you, Sarapis, who sit upon many unworked stones,
shall lie as a greatest ruin in thrice-wretched Egypt.
And all those of Egypt who directed desire toward you
shall bitterly weep for you, having considered you an immortal god in their minds;
as many as praised God will recognize that you are nothing.
And one of the priests, a linen-robed man, will say:
"Come, let us establish a beautiful precinct of the true God;
come, let us change the dreadful custom of our ancestors,
for the sake of which they performed processions and initiations
to gods of stone and earthenware, having no understanding.
Let us turn our souls, hymning the immortal God,
the Begetter himself, who is eternal,
the ruler of all, the true one, the King,
the soul-nourishing Father, the great God who exists forever."
And then in Egypt there shall be a great, holy temple,
and into it a God-fashioned people shall bring sacrifices,
and to them the immortal God will grant life.
But when the shameless tribes of Triballi abandon their land,
and the Ethiopians are about to cultivate their own Egypt,
they shall begin wickedness, so that all the latter things may come to pass.
For they will pull down the great temple of the Egyptian land;
and God will rain down terrible wrath upon the earth against them,
so as to destroy all the wicked and all the lawless.
And no longer will there be any sparing in that land,
because they did not keep what God had entrusted to them.
I saw the threat of the shining Sun among the stars,
and the terrible wrath of the Moon in the lightnings;
the stars travailed with battle, and God permitted them to fight.
For in place of the Sun long flames were waging strife,
and the two-horned rush of the Moon was altered;
the Morning Star engaged in battle, mounting the back of Leo;
Capricorn struck the tendon of the young Taurus;
and Taurus snatched away Capricorn's day of return.
And Orion removed Libra so that it remained no longer;
Virgo changed the lot of Gemini in Aries;
the Pleiad shone no longer, and Draco refused its belt;
Pisces penetrated into the girdle of Leo;
Cancer did not hold his ground, for he feared Orion;
Scorpio raised his tail against the dread Leo,
and the Dog slipped away from the flame of the Sun;
and the fury of mighty Phaenon set Aquarius ablaze.
Heaven itself arose, until it shook off the combatants;
and in its wrath it cast them headlong to the earth.
Swiftly struck down into the baths of Ocean,
they set the whole earth on fire; and the sky remained starless.
Book Six
From my heart I proclaim the great, renowned Son of the Immortal,
to whom the Most High Father gave a throne to receive
before he was yet born; since in twofold nature according to the flesh
he was raised up, washed in the streams of the river
Jordan, which is borne along with gray foot, sweeping its waves.
He who escapes the fire will be the first to see the sweet God
coming in the Spirit, on the white wings of a dove.
And a pure flower will bloom, and springs will gush forth.
I will show mortals the ways, and he will show the paths
of heaven; and he will teach everyone with wise words.
He will come to judgment and persuade a disobedient people,
boasting of his praiseworthy descent from his heavenly Father.
He will walk upon the waves, release men from sickness,
raise the dead, and drive away many pains;
and from a single basket there will be plenty of bread for men,
when the house of David brings forth a shoot; and in his hand
is the whole cosmos, earth and heaven and sea.
And he will flash like lightning upon the earth, just as once, when first revealed,
the two born from one another’s ribs saw him.
It will come to pass when the earth rejoices in the hope of the child.
Yet for you alone, land of Sodom, evil woes are in store;
for in your foolishness you did not recognize your God
when he came to mortal eyes; but from thorns
you plaited a crown for him, and mixed fearful gall
for insult and venom; this will bring evil woes upon you.
O blessed tree, on which God was stretched out,
earth shall not hold you, but you will behold heaven as your home,
when your fiery eye, O God, flashes like lightning.
From the Seventh Book
O wretched Rhodes, you first, indeed you I will bewail;
you will be the first of cities, and the first to perish,
bereft of men, and utterly destitute of livelihood.
Delos, you will drift and be unsettled upon the water;
Cyprus, the surge of the gray sea will one day destroy you;
Sicily, the fire burning against you will consume you.
This, I say, is the fearful and overflowing flood of God.
A certain Noah alone of all mortals escaped as a fugitive.
The earth will float, the mountains will float, and the sky will float.
All things will be water, and by water all things will perish.
The winds will cease, and there will be a second age.
O Phrygia, you will be the first to emerge above the surface of the water;
And you yourself will be the first into impiety to deny God,
gratifying speechless idols, which will destroy you, wretched one,
as many years revolve.
Wretched Ethiopians, having suffered pitiable griefs,
will be struck by swords, cowering beneath the blade.
Rich Egypt, ever caring for ears of grain,
which the Nile intoxicates with seven flowing streams,
civil strife with one another will destroy; and thence unexpectedly
men will drive out Apis, who is no god for men.
Alas, Laodicea! And you, having never seen God,
will lie, audacious one; and a wave of the Lycus will engulf you.
He himself, the begotten one, the great God, who
will make many stars, and will hang the central axis through the air,
and will set up a great terror for men to behold on high,
having measured out a pillar of great fire, whose drops
will destroy the evil races of destructive men.
For that time will once come, wherein mortals
will appease God, but they will not put an end to their unfulfilled
sorrows. But through the house of David all things are accomplished.
For to him God himself gave a throne, placing it in his hand;
and the messengers will slumber beneath his feet,
both those who display fires and those who show streams,
and those who preserve cities and those who send the winds.
And again a difficult life will come upon many mortals,
entering into souls and altering the minds of men.
But when a new shoot from the root puts forth buds,
the creation which once distributed abundant nourishment to all,
and these things will be more around [those] times. But when other
Persians, a race of warriors, begin to rule, straightway terrible
bridal chambers of maidens will exist because of lawless tribes.
For a mother will have her own son as husband; a son
will violate his mother; and a daughter, reclining with her father,
will sleep according to this barbarian custom; but later for them
Roman Ares will flash forth from many a spear;
and with human blood they will soak much earth.
And the champion of Italy will then flee from the spear's might.
And they will leave upon the earth a bloom engraved with gold,
going forth, bearing ever a sign of necessity.
Truly there will be a time when the whole wretched and ill-fated
Trojan land will drink up a tomb, not a wedding, where deep
brides will weep, because indeed they did not perceive God,
but ever gave forth sound with drums and clapping.
Prophesy, Colophon! A great and fearful fire hangs over you.
Ill-wed Thessaly, the earth will look upon you no more,
nor even your ashes, but you will sail alone, a fugitive from the mainland.
O wretched one, you will be a dismal refuse of war for them,
having fallen to dogs and rivers and swords.
O wretched Corinth, you around her will receive grievous Ares,
wretched one, and you will perish at each other's hands.
Tyre, what great things indeed you alone will receive! For of the pious
bereft of men, she will pull through in her folly.
Ah, Coele-Syria, last among the Phoenician people,
upon whom the Berytian brine lies surging,
wretched one, you did not recognize your God, whom once
Jordan washed in third parts, and the Spirit flew as a dove,
who beforehand was Creator of both earth and starry heaven,
the Word with the Father and the Holy Spirit,
and having put on flesh, quickly flew to his Father’s house.
And great Heaven established three towers for him,
in which now dwell the noble mothers of God:
Hope, Piety, and beloved Reverence,
delighting not in gold or silver, but in the reverence
of human beings, and sacrifices, and most righteous thoughts.
And you shall offer sacrifice to the immortal, great, exalted God,
not melting a grain of frankincense with fire, nor with a knife
slaying a shaggy-fleeced ram, but together with all
who share your blood, taking wild winged birds,
and having prayed, you shall send them forth, stretching your eyes toward heaven;
and you shall pour water as a libation upon pure fire, crying out thus:
"As the Father begot you as the Word, O Father, I have released a bird,
the Word, a swift messenger of words, with holy waters
sprinkling your baptism, through which you shone forth from fire."
Nor shall you shut your door whenever another stranger
comes to you in need, to ward off poverty and hunger.
Rather, taking the head of this man and sprinkling it with water,
pray three times; and to your God cry out aloud in this manner:
"I do not desire wealth; simple as I am, I received a simple man;
grant to both of us, O Father; hear us, O Provider!"
To you when you pray he will give; and thereafter the man has gone away.
Do not afflict me, holy and righteous reverence of God,
pure, unenslaved, proven concerning the race...
Sustain my wretched heart, Father; for I look
unto you, the Undefiled One, whom human hands did not fashion.
Sardinia, you who are now heavy, shall be changed into ashes.
And you shall no longer be an island, when the tenth period arrives.
Sailors shall seek you upon the waters when you exist no more,
and halcyons shall wail a pitiful lament over you.
Rugged Mygdonia, beacon of the sea hard to pass,
you will boast of an age, but throughout the ages you shall perish
entirely by a scorching wind, and you will be driven mad with many sorrows.
Celtic land, along your mountain, by the impassable Alps,
deep sand shall bury you completely; you shall no longer yield tribute,
neither ear of grain nor pasturage; and you will be utterly desolate of peoples
forever, and growing thick with freezing ice,
you shall pay the penalty for the outrage which you did not perceive, unholy one.
Stout-hearted Rome, after the Macedonian spear
you will flash like lightning into Olympus; but God will make you wholly forgotten,
at the very time when you seem far more securely to the eye
to remain steadfast; then I will cry out to you such words:
Perishing, you will one day utter a clear cry, and a gleaming ruin...
A second time, Rome, again a second time I am about to speak to you.
And now, wretched Syria, I bewail you piteously.
Ill-counseled Thebes, an evil sound will come upon you
from sounding pipes; to you the trumpet will sound an evil blast,
it will sound, and you will see the whole land perishing.
Alas for you, wretched one, alas, malignant sea!
You will be entirely devoured by fire, and you will destroy the people with brine.
For there will be such raging fire upon the earth,
as great as water, and it will flow and destroy the whole earth.
It will burn mountains, scorch rivers, and drain springs.
The world will become an unworld as human beings perish.
And burning miserably, the wretched will then look up to
heaven, exhausted not with stars, but in fire.
Nor do they perish swiftly, but while their flesh is destroyed,
burned by the blast for years of ages,
they will forever in severe torments know the law of God,
that it cannot be eluded; and the violated earth,
whatever sacrifice it daringly and falsely received on the altars of gods,
has seen smoke rising painfully through the air.
And those will endure excessive suffering who for the sake of gain
will prophesy shameful things, fostering an evil time.
They who put on the shaggy fleece of sheep
will falsely call themselves Hebrews, a lineage they have not received,
but babbling with words over griefs for profit,
they will not change their way of life and will not persuade the righteous,
who propitiate God with all faithfulness in their heart.
And in the third allotment of revolving years
of the first ogdoad, another world is seen again.
There will be night everywhere . . . long and unyielding.
And then a terrible smell of sulfur will encircle all,
announcing slaughters, when those perish
both by night and by famine; then he will generate a pure mind
in human beings, and will establish your race, as it was formerly for you;
no longer will anyone cut a deep furrow with a curved plow;
oxen will not plunge the guiding iron downward;
there will be no vine branches nor ear of grain, but all together
will eat the dewy manna with white teeth.
And God will also be with them then, who will teach you,
even as he taught me, wretched one. For whatever evils I formerly did
knowingly, and many other evils I wickedly wrought in neglect:
countless bridal beds were mine, but no marriage was cared for;
and to all, entirely faithless, I brought a wild oath.
I shut out those in need, and going among those coming forward,
into a like valley I did not perceive the utterance of God.
Therefore fire has consumed me and will consume me; for neither will I myself
live, but an evil time will destroy me, where a tomb for me
mortals passing by the sea will construct.
And they will destroy me with stones; for speaking concerning my Father
I imparted his beloved Son. Cast stones at me, cast stones, all of you!
For thus I will live, and fix my eyes upon heaven.
Book Eight
When great wrath comes upon a disobedient world,
in the last age I make known the wrathful judgments of God,
prophesying to all human beings from city to city.
From the time when the tower fell and the tongues of men
were divided into many dialects of mortals,
first was the kingdom of Egypt, then that of the Persians,
of the Medes and Ethiopians, and of Assyrian Babylon,
then of Macedonia, boasting in great pride,
and then fifth, the famous, lawless kingdom of the Italians
will at the last show many evils to all mortals,
and will consume the toils of people of the whole earth.
It will lead untiring kings of the nations to the west,
and will lay down laws for the peoples and subject all things.
Late do the mills of God grind the fine meal.
Then fire will destroy all things, and reduce to fine dust
the peaks of the high-crested mountains and all flesh.
Love of money and folly are the beginning of all evils;
for there will be a lust for deceitful gold and silver.
For mortals preferred nothing greater than these,
neither the light of the sun, nor heaven, nor the sea,
nor the broad-backed earth, from which all things grow,
nor God who gives all things, the begetter of all,
nor did they prefer faith in these things and piety.
A fountain of impiety and a guide to disorder,
an engine of wars, a hostile torment to peace,
making parents enemies to children, and children to parents.
Nor will marriage ever be held in honor at all apart from gold.
The land will have boundaries, and the whole sea guards,
divided deceitfully among all who possess gold;
wishing to possess the all-nourishing earth for ages,
they will plunder the poor, so that they themselves,
having acquired more land, may enslave them in their arrogance.
And if the monstrous earth did not have its seat far
from the starry heaven, the light would not be equal for men,
but bought with gold it would belong to the rich,
and God would have prepared another world for the poor.
A matching heavenly blow will one day come upon you from above, haughty Rome,
and you will bend your neck first,
and you will be leveled to the ground, and fire will utterly consume you,
cast down upon your own foundations, and your wealth will perish,
and wolves and foxes will inhabit your foundations.
And then you will be wholly desolate, as though you had never existed.
Where then is the Palladium? What sort of god will save you,
whether of gold, stone, or bronze? Or where then for you
are the decrees of the Senate? Where the offspring of Rhea or of Cronus
or of Zeus, and of all the lifeless demons whom you worshipped,
phantoms of the weary dead,
whose tombs ill-fated Crete will possess as a boast,
performing rites of enthronement for senseless corpses?
But when fifteen kings have arisen for you, luxurious one,
having enslaved the world from east to west,
there will be a gray-headed ruler bearing the name of the near sea,
inspecting the world with defiling foot, providing gifts,
having very much gold and gathering more silver of enemies,
and having stripped them, he will depart.
And he will partake in all the mysteries of magical shrines;
he will display a boy as a god, he will dissolve all sanctuaries,
and from the beginning he will open to all the mysteries of deception.
A time of lamentation will follow, when Aelius himself shall perish.
And once a people will say: 'Your great power, O city, will fall,'
knowing at once the impending evil day that is approaching.
And then they will mourn together, foreseeing your
most pitiable doom, fathers and infant children;
mournful, they will lament dirges beside the banks of the Tiber.
After him three will rule, holding the very last day,
fulfilling the name of the heavenly God,
whose power is both now and for all ages.
One, being an old man, will hold the scepter for a long time,
a most pitiable king, who will shut up all the wealth of the world
in his house, guarding it, so that whenever
the fugitive matricide returns flashing from the ends of the earth,
giving these things to all, he will bestow great wealth on Asia.
And then you will mourn, having stripped off the broad-purple
radiance of rulers and wearing a garment of mourning,
O boastful queen, offspring of Latin Rome;
no longer will you have the renown of your boastfulness,
nor will you ever be raised up, ill-fated one, but you will be brought low;
for the glory of the eagle-bearing legions will also fall.
Where then is your power? What land will be an ally,
having been enslaved unlawfully by your foolish pursuits?
For there will then be confusion among the mortals of the whole earth,
whenever the Almighty himself comes to judge upon the tribunal
the souls of the living and the dead and the entire world.
Neither will parents be dear to children, nor children to parents,
because of impiety and unhoped-for tribulation.
From then on there will be gnashing for you, and scattering, and capture,
whenever the fall of cities and chasms of the earth arrive;
and whenever a purple dragon comes upon the waves,
having a multitude in its belly, and will nourish your children
in the time of approaching famine and civil war,
near is the end of the world and the final day,
and the judgment of the immortal God for the approved chosen ones.
And first there will be inexorable wrath for the Romans;
a blood-drinking season and a wretched life will come.
Alas for you, Italian land, great barbarian nation,
you did not perceive whence you came naked and unworthy
to the light of the sun, so that to that very same place
you might return naked, and afterwards enter into judgment,
as having judged unjustly . . .
By gigantic hands alone throughout the entire world,
coming down from on high, you will dwell beneath the earth.
With naphtha and asphalt and brimstone and much fire
you will be utterly destroyed and will become burning dust
for ages; and everyone who looks on will hear
a great, mournful bellowing and gnashing of teeth from Hades,
and you beating your godless breast with your own hands.
Night is equal alike for all, both for those possessing wealth
and for the poor; naked from the earth, and naked back to the earth
they arrive and cease, having completed the span of life.
There is no slave there, nor master, nor tyrant,
no kings, nor leaders full of great conceit,
no legal orator, no ruler judging for money;
nor do they pour out blood with libations of sacrifices on altars;
the tambourine does not sound, nor the cymbal . . .
nor the multi-holed flute, having a mind-ruining tone,
nor the piping carrying an imitation of a crooked serpent,
nor the trumpet, the barbarous-voiced messenger of wars;
nor are they drunk with lawless carousals, nor with choral dances;
no sound of the lyre, no evil-working device;
there is no strife, no multifaceted wrath, nor sword
among the dead, but an eternity common to all.—
The keeper of the keys of the great prison at the judgment seat of God.—
Adorn yourselves with golden, silver, and stone images,
make yourselves lovely, so that you may come to the bitter day,
to behold your first punishment, O Rome, and gnashing of teeth.
And no longer will anyone place their neck under your slavish yoke,
no Syrian, no Greek, no barbarian, no other nation.
You will be thoroughly despoiled and held to account for all you did,
and you will give in payment, wailing in terror, until you pay back everything;
and you will be a triumph for the world and a reproach to all.—
From that time the sixth generation of Latin kings
will fulfill their final life and abandon the scepter.
Another king from the same generation will reign,
who will rule over all the earth and hold the scepters,
and he will rule with absolute authority by the counsels of the most high God;
children and the generation of children of this unshaken ruler;
for so it is decreed by revolving time,
whenever there shall be thrice five kings of Egypt.
Then, whenever the five-century phoenix arrives—
he will come to lay waste the race of peoples, the undiscerning tribes,
the nation of the Hebrews. Then Ares will plunder Ares;
he himself will destroy the arrogant threat of the Romans.
For then the flourishing empire of Rome perished,
the ancient queen over many neighboring peoples.
No longer may the plain of luxuriant Rome prevail,
whenever he comes conquering from Asia with Ares.
And having done all these things, he will come to the founded city.
And thrice three hundred and forty-eight
years you will complete, when your ill-fated time comes upon you
fate compelling, having fulfilled your name.
Alas for me, thrice-wretched! When will I ever see that day
of yours, O Rome, and especially for all Latins?
Revel, if you wish, in him who in secret birth
mounted the Trojan chariot from the land of Asia,
having the heart of a fiery beast. But when he cuts through the isthmus,
gazing about, advancing against all, having crossed the sea,
then also dark blood will pursue the great beast.
And a hound pursued the lion that was destroying shepherds;
they will take away his scepter, and he will depart into Hades.
To the Rhodians also will come an evil, the last, yet the greatest;
and for Thebes an evil capture remains thereafter.
And Egypt will perish through the wickedness of her rulers.
[And whatever mortals afterward escaped headlong destruction,
thrice-blessed and four times happy was that man.]
Rome also shall become a ruin, and Delos unseen,
and Samos sand — — — — — — —
Afterward, moreover, disaster will come upon the Persians
in return for their arrogance; all insolence will perish.
And then the holy King will hold the scepters of the whole earth
for all ages, having raised the dead.
May the Most High then bring three to a pitiable fate for Rome,
and all men will perish in their own homes;
yet they will not be persuaded, which would be far better.
But when he increases for all the evil day
of famine and unbearable plague and battle turmoil,
then once again the wretched ruler of old,
having assembled a council, will deliberate how he may destroy —
dry things will bloom, appearing together with leaves;
and the heavenly foundation will show upon the solid rock
rain, fire, and strong winds upon the earth,
and an abundance of poisons for crops throughout the entire earth. —
Yet they will act again possessing a shameless spirit,
fearing neither the wrath of God nor of men,
forsaking reverence, craving shamelessness,
tyrants in dissensions, sinners and violent men,
liars, friends of the faithless, workers of evil, in no way truthful,
faith-destroyers, phrase-coiners, pouring forth blasphemies;
nor will they have any satiety of wealth, but shamelessly
they will amass more; having been tyrannized, they will perish.
All the stars will fall headlong into the sea,
many stars in succession, and the radiant comet
men will call the star, a sign of great distress
approaching, of war and slaughter.
May I never live when the defiled woman reigns,
but then, when heavenly grace reigns supreme,
and when at last the holy Child, destroying all deceits,
shall utterly destroy, opening the ruinous abyss with bonds,
and a wooden house suddenly covers mortals around.
But when the tenth generation enters within the house of Hades,
Then great power will belong to a female, for whom many evils
God himself will increase, when she happens to be crowned
with royal honor; and throughout the year it will be a gentle age.
The sun, running parched, shines by night,
and the stars will abandon the pole; and raging with a great tempest
it will desolate the earth; and there will be a resurrection of the dead.
The running of the lame will be most swift, and the deaf will hear,
and the blind will see, and those who do not speak will speak,
and there will be a common life and wealth for all.
The earth will belong equally to all, divided neither by walls
nor by fences, and it will then bear more abundant fruit,
and springs of sweet wine, white milk,
and honey it will give . . .
and the judgment of immortal God . . .
but when God changes the seasons . . .
making winter into summer, then all divine oracles will be fulfilled.
But when the world has perished . . .
JESUS CHRIST, SON OF GOD, SAVIOR, CROSS.
The earth will sweat, when the sign of judgment will come.
And from heaven will come the King who is to be through the ages,
present in person to judge all flesh and the whole world.
Both faithful and faithless mortal men will see God,
the Most High with his holy ones at the end of time.
And he will judge the souls of flesh-bearing humans at his tribunal,
when the whole world becomes waste land and thorns.
And mortals will cast away their idols and all their wealth.
And the fire will burn up earth, heaven, and sea,
as it searches out everything, and it will break the gates of the prison of Hades.
Then all flesh of the dead will come into the free light
of the holy ones; but fire will convict the lawless forever.
Whatever deeds anyone did in secret, then he will tell all;
for God will open dark breasts to the luminaries.
And there will be wailing from all and gnashing of teeth.
The brilliance of the sun and the dances of the stars will fail.
He will roll up the heaven; and the moon's light will perish.
He will raise up valleys, and destroy the heights of mountains,
and grievous height will no longer appear among human beings.
Mountains will be level with plains, and every sea
will no longer have navigation; for the earth will then be parched
together with its springs, and bubbling rivers will fail.
And a trumpet from heaven will utter a voice of much lamentation,
wailing over the defilement of wretched deeds and the woes of the world.
And then the earth, yawning open, will expose Tartarean chaos.
And all will come to the judgment seat of God the King.
And a river of fire and sulfur will flow from heaven.
Then there will be a sign for all mortals, a distinguished seal:
the wood among the faithful, the longed-for horn,
the life of pious men, but a stumbling block to the world,
enlightening the called with waters at twelve springs;
an iron rod shepherding them will indeed prevail.
This is our God, now described beforehand in acrostics,
the immortal Savior King, who suffered for our sake;
whom Moses prefigured, stretching out his pure arms,
conquering Amalek through faith, so that the people might know
that he is chosen and precious before God the Father,
the rod of David and the stone which he promised,
in whom whoever believes will have eternal life.
For not in glory, but as a mortal will he come into creation,
pitiable, dishonored, formless, so that he may give hope to the pitiable;
and he will give form to corruptible flesh, and heavenly faith
to the faithless, and he will fashion the man
molded from the beginning by the holy hands of God,
whom the serpent deceitfully led astray to depart to the fate
of death and to receive the knowledge of good and evil,
so that, abandoning God, he served mortal ways.
For taking him first of all as his counselor from the beginning,
the Almighty said: "Let us both, Child, make
the mortal tribes, modeled after our image;
now I with hands, but you later with the word will heal
our form, so that we may give a common resurrection."
Mindful therefore of this counsel, he will come into creation,
bearing a corresponding likeness into a pure virgin,
illuminating with water through the hands of an elder,
doing all things by a word, and healing every disease.
He will still the winds with a word, and calm the raging
sea, treading it with feet of peace and in faith.
And from five loaves together with fish from the sea,
he will satisfy five thousand men in the desert,
and taking then all the leftover fragments,
he will fill twelve baskets for the hope of the peoples.
And he will call the souls of the blessed, and love the pitiable,
who, though mocked, will do good in return for evil,
being beaten, being scourged, longing for poverty.
Perceiving all things, seeing all things, and hearing all things,
he will search inner hearts and lay them bare for conviction;
for he himself is the hearing and mind and sight of all things,
and the Word who fashions forms, whom all things obey,
both saving the dead and healing every disease.
Afterwards he will come into the hands of the lawless and faithless,
and with unclean hands they will give blows to God,
and with defiled mouths poisonous spittle.
And he will give his back, spreading it out then to scourges;
[for he will deliver a pure virgin to the world.]
And being struck with fists he will keep silent, lest anyone recognize
who he is, whose son he is, and whence he came, that he might speak to the dead.
And he will wear the crown of thorns; for from thorns
the crown of the elect is an everlasting glory.
They will pierce his ribs with a reed on account of their law;
for from reeds shaken by an alien spirit
wrath and retribution were nurtured for the judgments of the soul.
But when all these things which I spoke are accomplished,
then every law is dissolved in him, which from the beginning
was given to mortals in ordinances because of a disobedient people.
He will stretch out his hands and measure the whole world.
And for food they gave gall, and vinegar to drink;
this table of inhospitality they will show.
And the veil of the temple will be rent, and at midday
there will be a monstrous dark night for three hours.
For it was shown that to serve no longer in hidden law and temple,
veiled in the worldly apparitions,
when the eternal Master descended to earth.
And he will come to Hades, proclaiming hope to all
the holy ones, the end of the ages and the final day,
and he will fulfill the destiny of death, having slept for three days;
and then departing from the dead he will come into the light,
being the first to show the beginning of resurrection to the called,
having washed away with the waters of an immortal spring
the former evils, so that being born from above
they might no longer be enslaved to the lawless customs of the world.
And first then the Lord will appear visibly to his own
in the flesh, as he was before, and in his hands and feet he will show
the four marks pierced in his own limbs,
east and west and south and north;
for so many kingdoms of the world will execute
the unlawful, blameworthy deed, for a type for us.
Rejoice, pure daughter of Zion, having suffered many things;
your King himself, mounted upon a colt, enters,
appearing gentle to all, that he might take up our yoke,
servile and hard to bear, lying upon the neck,
and dissolve godless laws and violent bonds.
Know him to be your God, the Son of God;
glorifying him and holding him in your breast,
love him from your soul, and bear his name.
Cast off the former things, and wash yourself in his blood;
for he is not propitiated by your songs nor by prayers,
nor does he heed corruptible sacrifices, being himself incorruptible;
but uttering a hymn from discerning mouths,
know who this is, and then you will see the Begetter.
Then in time all the elements of the cosmos will be made desolate,
air, earth, sea, the light of blazing fire;
and the heavenly vault and night and all the days
will collapse into one, and into an utterly desolate form.
For all the stars among the luminaries will fall from heaven.
And no longer will swift-winged birds fly through the air,
nor any step tread the earth, for all wild beasts will perish.
And there will be no voices of men, nor of wild beasts, nor of winged birds.
The cosmos, becoming disordered, will hear no useful sound;
but the deep sea will roar with a great sound of threat,
and all the swimming creatures of the sea, trembling, will die;
and no longer will a ship carrying cargo sail upon the waves.
And the earth, bloodied by wars, will groan aloud;
and all the souls of men will gnash with their teeth,
[the souls of the lawless with wailing and fear,]
melting away with thirst, famine, plague, and slaughter;
and they will call death fair, but it will flee from them;
for death will no longer give them rest, nor will night;
and they will pray much in vain to God who rules on high,
and then he will openly turn his face away from them.
For he gave seven ages of repentance
to wandering mortals through the hands of a pure virgin.
God himself showed all these things in my mind,
and through my mouth he will accomplish all that has been spoken:
"I know the number of the sand and the measures of the sea;
I know the recesses of the earth and misty Tartarus;
I know the numbers of the stars, and the trees, and how many tribes
of quadrupeds, swimming creatures, and winged birds exist,
and of articulate mortals, both those who are and the dead who are yet to be;
for I myself fashioned the forms and the mind of men,
and I gave upright speech and taught understanding,
having fashioned eyes and ears, seeing and hearing,
perceiving every thought and knowing all things;
being within, I keep silent, and later I myself will convict them,
[and exacting vengeance for whatever anyone did in secret among mortals,
coming even to the judgment seat of God to speak to mortals.]
And I understand the mute and hear one who speaks not,
and I know how great the whole height is from earth to heaven;
I know the beginning and the end, I who created heaven and earth.
[For all things are from him; he knows the things from the beginning to the end.]
For I alone am God, and there is no other God.
They pronounce oracles before an image of me fashioned from matter,
and having formed a voiceless idol with their own hands,
they glorify it with prayers and unholy rites.
Having abandoned the Creator, they have served licentiousness,
and though all have received from him, they give gifts to useless things,
and they suppose all these useful things to be honors for me,
filling them with savor at the feast, as for their own dead.
For they burn flesh and marrow-filled bones,
sacrificing on altars, and pour out blood to demons;
and they light lamps to me, the one who gives light,
and as to a thirsty god mortals pour libations of wine,
drunken to no purpose over useless idols.
I have no need of your sacrifice or libation,
nor of defiling savor, nor of most hateful blood.
For in memory of kings and tyrants
they will do these things for dead spirits, as though heavenly beings,
performing a godless and ruinous worship.
And godless men call their images gods,
having abandoned the Creator, and believing that they have
all hope and life from them, deaf and speechless things;
faithful to evil, they are ignorant of the good end."
I myself set forth two ways, of life and of death,
and set before their judgment to choose the good life;
yet they rushed toward death and eternal fire.
Man is my image, possessing right reason;
for him set a pure and bloodless table,
having filled it with good things, and give bread to the hungry,
and drink to the thirsty, and garments for the naked body,
providing from your own labors with pure hands.
Receive the afflicted and stand by the weary,
and offer a living sacrifice to me, the Living One,
sowing now upon the water, so that I also will one day give you
immortal fruits, and you shall have eternal light
and unfading life, when I test all people with fire.
For I will smelt all things and separate them into purity;
I will roll up heaven, I will open the recesses of the earth,
and then I will raise the dead, dissolving fate
and the sting of death, and afterward I will come to judgment,
judging the life of pious and impious mortals;
and I will set ram against ram, and shepherd against shepherd,
and calf against calf near one another for testing;
whoever were exalted, being convicted under examination,
and stopped every mouth, so that in their jealousy
they might likewise enslave those who act uprightly,
commanding them to be silent, rushing after gain.
And all the approved shall then find a place with me,
and no longer henceforth will you say in grief, 'It will be tomorrow,'
nor 'It happened yesterday'; you will not be anxious about many days,
nor spring, nor winter, nor indeed summer, nor autumn,
nor sunset, nor sunrise; for I will make an endless day.
And into eternity the longed-for light shall be.
Self-begotten, undefiled, ever-flowing, and eternal,
holding the heavens, measuring in his might the fiery breath,
and he holds the scepter of the crash with harsh fire,
and calms the roar of heavy-sounding thunder,
shaking the earth, he restrains the rushing whirlwinds...
and blunts the fire-gleaming scourges of lightning,
and holds the unspeakable torrents of rain and the blasts of hail,
the frosty clouds' shafts, and the onsets of winter.
For they themselves determine all things in their mind,
as many things as seem good to you yourself and you nod assent to do.
To your Child, existing before all creation with equal heart
as counselor, former of mortal men and creator of life,
whom you addressed with the first sweet utterance of your mouth:
'Behold, let us make man altogether like our form,
and give him life-sustaining breath to hold;
though he is mortal, all worldly things shall serve him,
and though formed of dust, we will subject all things to him.'
These things you spoke to the Logos, and in your mind all things were fashioned;
and all the elements together obeyed your command,
and eternal creation was marshaled together for the mortal creature,
heaven, air, fire, earth, dry land, and the surge of the sea,
sun, moon, chorus of stars, [mountains . . .]
night, day, sleep, waking, spirit, and impulse,
soul and understanding, craft, voice, and strength,
and the wild tribes of animals, those that swim and those that fly,
those on foot, amphibious, creeping, and of two-fold nature;
for all things were arranged by yourself under your guidance.
And in the last times he visited the earth, and coming in lowliness,
a new light arose from the womb of the Virgin Mary,
and coming from heaven he put on mortal form.
First, then, Gabriel was revealed in his strong, holy form;
and second, the archangel spoke to the maiden with his voice:
“Receive God, O virgin, in your undefiled womb.”
Having thus spoken, God breathed grace into the maiden;
and then both dread and wonder seized her as she listened,
and she stood trembling; her mind was startled,
her heart throbbing at the unfamiliar message.
Yet again she rejoiced, and her heart was cheered by his voice,
and she smiled with maidenly joy, and blushed upon her cheek,
delighting in gladness and charmed in her mind with modesty,
and courage came upon her. And the Word flew into her womb,
and becoming incarnate in time and brought to life in the belly,
was fashioned in mortal likeness and became a boy
through a virgin birth; for this is a great wonder to mortals,
yet no great wonder to God the Father and God the Son.
And at the birth of the infant, joy flew toward the earth,
and the heavenly throne laughed, and the cosmos exulted.
A newly shining, divine star was revered by the Magi,
and wrapped in swaddling clothes, the infant in a manger was shown to God-fearing
ox-drivers and goatherds and shepherds of lambs;
and Bethlehem was proclaimed the God-called homeland of the Word.
And to be humble in heart, to hate bitter ends,
and above all to love one’s neighbor as oneself;
and to love God with all one’s soul, and to serve him.
Therefore we, being born of the holy, heavenly offspring
of Christ, are called his kin,
holding a remembrance of gladness in our worship,
walking the paths of piety and truth.
We are never permitted to approach the inner shrines of temples,
nor to pour libations to carved images, nor to honor them with vows,
nor with delightful fragrances of flowers, nor with the gleams
of lamps, nor indeed to adorn them with votive offerings,
nor with vapors of frankincense sending up a flame on the altar;
nor with bull-slaying sacrifices to send forth the blood of slaughtered sheep in libations,
rejoicing in ransoms, appeasements for earthly punishment;
nor from a flesh-devouring pyre with savory smoke
and defiling blasts to pollute the radiance of the upper air;
but rejoicing with pure minds and a cheerful spirit,
and with abundant acts of love and generous hands,
with soothing psalms and songs befitting God,
We bid men to hymn you as imperishable and truthful,
God, the all-begetter, wise-minded . . .
Eleventh Oracle of the Sibyl
O world of widely scattered mortals, and high walls,
and insatiable cities and countless nations
of the East and West and South and North,
divided among diverse tongues and kingdoms:
truly, the worst of your woes I am about to declare.
For ever since the flood came upon the men of old
and destroyed the wretched generation with many waters,
the Almighty himself provided another race
of unwearied men; who, setting themselves against heaven,
built a tower to an unspeakable height; but on each other
their tongues were loosed in turn; and the wrath came upon them,
hurled from the Most High God, and the tower fell,
immense; for they stirred up evil strife against one another.
Then indeed it was the tenth generation of articulate men
from when these things occurred; and the whole earth was divided
among men of foreign lands and diverse dialects,
whose numbers I will tell, and I will name them with acrostics
of the initial letter, and make known the name.
And first Egypt will receive royal rule,
eminent and just; and then men within it,
many counselors, will rule over it; but afterwards
a terrible man will rule, a mightier close-fighting warrior;
and he will have the letter of the acrostic for a name,
and will stretch out swords against pious people.
And there will be a great sign for him while he holds sway
in the land of Egypt, which, greatly exalting itself,
will then provide grain for souls perishing in famine;
he will nourish the East and the race of Assyrian men,
he, a prisoner himself, the judge; and know his name
is of the measure of the tenth number.
But whenever a ten-fold plague from shining heaven
comes upon Egypt, then I will cry out these things to you again:
"Alas for you, Memphis, alas, great kingdom;
the Red Sea shall destroy a great multitude of your people!"
Then whenever they leave the fruitful plain of destruction,
the twelve-tribed people commanded by the Immortal,
the Sovereign God himself will also give a law to men.
And then a great, stout-hearted king will rule over the Hebrews,
having a name from sandy Egypt,
a Theban man of false homeland; and he will love Memphis,
a terrible serpent, and will take great precautions in wars.
When the twelfth decade of the kingdom is coming round,
and of the seventeenth century of years, when another
five remain, then indeed shall be the rule of Persia.
And then darkness will be upon the Judeans, nor will they escape
famine and intolerable pestilence on that day.
But whenever the Persian rules and leaves the scepter,
a son of a grandson as the years revolve
unto only five tetrads; and he shall tithe these,
having completed a hundred enneads, and you will pay for everything.
And then you, Perseis, will be a servant given over to the Medes,
perishing by blows through fierce battles.
Immediately there will be evil for the Persians and the Assyrians,
and for all Egypt, and Libya, and the Ethiopians,
and for the Carians and Pamphylians, and for all other mortals.
And then he will give the royal rule to grandsons,
who in turn will lay waste nations with much plunder,
snatching away the whole earth without pity.
The wretched Persians by the Tigris will lament dirges of woe.
Egypt will water much land with tears.
And then for you, Median land, many evils will he bring,
the Indian-born, wealthy king, until you pay for all things
whatever you did before, having a shameless spirit.
Alas for you, Median nation! Afterwards you will be enslaved
to Ethiopian men beyond the land of Meroe;
adding seven years to a hundred from the beginning,
you will fulfill them, wretched one, and place your neck under the yoke.
And then a dark-skinned, gray-haired, great-hearted
Indian king will arise thereafter, who will inflict many evils
upon the East through fierce battles;
and he will maltreat you indeed, and destroy you more than all others.
But when he has reigned for twenty and ten years,
and seven besides ten, then indeed from royal rule
every nation will run wild with frenzy and display freedom,
leaving behind slavish blood for three units of years.
Yet again he will come and will place under the yoke the neck
of every nation of men, again by force, just as before
when it was serving the king, and it will submit willingly.
There will be great peace throughout the whole world.
And then a great man will be king for the Assyrians;
he will rule and persuade all to speak what is pleasing to the heart,
whatever things God lawfully ordained; and then before him
all kings boasting in spear-points will tremble,
fearful and speechless, and exceedingly mighty, charming leaders
will serve him because of the counsels of the great God.
For by his word he will persuade all things and subject all things,
and the temple of the great God and the lovely altar
he himself will build stoutly, and will cast down the idols;
and tribes, and the generation of fathers, and infant children,
bringing them together into one, he will settle them as inhabitants;
and he will have a name of the number two hundred,
he will show the signs of the eighteenth letter.
But when he has ruled for revolving decades,
two and five besides, coming to the end of time,
there will be as many kings as there are tribes of mortals,
as many clans, and as many cities, and as many islands,
continents of the blessed, and bright-fruited fields.
And one great king will be the leader of these men;
and many high-spirited kings will yield to him,
and to him, his children, and his very wealthy grandsons
they will grant portions for the sake of royal rule,
for eighty decades, and in addition to these
six units of years; he will rule, and at the end they will rise in opposition.
When a mighty beast comes with powerful Ares,
then wrath will spring up against you, queenly land.
Alas for you, Persian land, how great an outpouring
of human blood you will receive, when that
strong-spirited man comes to you; then again I will cry out these things.
But when Italy brings forth a great wonder for mortals,
the whimpering of babes beside a pure spring,
in a shady cave, children of a sheep-eating beast,
who, having grown to manhood upon seven mighty hills,
will cast down headlong many who possess a shameless spirit,
both numbering a hundred, whose name will show
a great sign of things to come; and on seven hills
they will build strong walls and set grievous Ares about them.
And then again there will be an insurrection of men
arising around you, great land of fair ears of grain,
high-spirited Egypt; yet again I will cry out these things.
Moreover, you will receive a great blow in your houses,
and again you will have an insurrection of your own men.
And now, wretched Phrygia, I lament for you piteously;
for capture will come upon you from horse-taming Hellas,
and a terrible war through fierce conflicts.
Ilion, I pity you; for an Erinys from Sparta
will come to your halls, blended with a baneful star;
and especially for you she will bring toils, distress, groans, and wailing,
whenever men well skilled in battle begin the fight,
heroes far the best of the war-loving Greeks.
And one of these will be a king, a mighty spearman;
on behalf of his brother he will pursue the foulest deeds.
And they in turn will destroy the Phrygians' famous walls of Troy,
when, as twice five years revolve,
the Son of Kronos fulfills the murderous deeds of war,
and suddenly a wooden house encloses mortals,
and this you will receive upon your knees, not perceiving,
O heavily grieving one, that it is pregnant with an ambush of Greeks;
alas, in a single night how many Hades will receive,
and how much plunder of the much-weeping old man
he will carry off; and ageless will be his fame among those to come.
And the great king, a man from Zeus, will hold a name
from the first letter; and when he attains his homecoming,
then indeed he will fall by the hand of a treacherous woman.
And from the lineage and blood of Assaracus will rule
a renowned child of heroes, a mighty and valiant man.
And he will come from Troy laid waste by great fire,
fleeing from his fatherland because of the fearful turmoil of Ares;
carrying his aged father on his shoulders,
and holding his only son by the hand, he will perform a pious deed,
looking about, [who cleaved the fury of the fire
of burning Troy,] and pressing through the throng,
in dread he will cross over the land and the fearful sea.
And he will bear a three-syllable name; for not obscure
is the initial letter that signifies this preeminent man.
And then he will raise up a city and the mighty nation of the Latins.
In his fifteenth year, upon the depths of the briny sea,
perishing in the waters, he will reach the end of death.
Yet not even in death will the races of mortal men forget him;
for his offspring hereafter shall rule over all,
as far as the region between the Euphrates and Tigris rivers
in the land of the Assyrians, wherever the Parthian extended his reach.
This shall be for generations to come, whenever all these things come to pass.
And again there will be a certain elderly man, a wise singer,
whom all will call the wisest among mortal men,
by whose noble wits the whole world will be instructed;
for he will write comprehensively with power and understanding.
And he will clearly write many ineffable things, now here, now there,
having mastered my words, measures, and verses;
for he himself will be the very first to unfold my books,
and afterward he will conceal them and no longer show them to men
until the end of baneful death, the finish of his life.
But when indeed these things have been fulfilled, which I have spoken,
the Greeks will fight against one another once again;
Assyrians and Arabs and quiver-bearing Medes,
Persians and Sicilians and Lydians will rise up,
Thracians and Bithynians, and those who beside the streams of the Nile
dwell in the land of fair wheat; and into their midst turmoil
the imperishable God will place for them all together. But most terribly,
a bastard Assyrian man, an Ethiopian, will come suddenly,
having the heart of a beast; and looking around, he will cut through every isthmus,
and advancing against all, he will sail across the sea.
And then very many things will happen to you, faithless Hellas.
Alas for you, wretched Hellas, how much you must lament!
For eighty-seven revolving years
you will be the wretched refuse of a fearful, all-tribal war.
Then again there will be woe for Hellas from the Macedonians,
and he will destroy all Thrace and bring the toil of Ares
upon the islands and the continents and the war-loving lands.
He will be among the frontline fighters, and this name he will bear,
which the letter numbering fifty ten times reveals.
He will have a short-lived rule; but a very great
and boundless kingdom he will leave behind across the earth.
Yet he himself in turn will fall by an ill-counseling spearman,
having lived in Syria, ruling as no one else had.
And thereafter his high-spirited son will rule in turn,
of the initial letter; and there will be an end of his race.
They will not truly call him a son of Zeus, nor of Ammon,
all alike, and they will fashion him as a bastard son of the Son of Cronos.
And he in turn will sack the cities of many mortal men;
and for Europe a very great sore will shoot up.
This one will also ravage the city of Babylon with pestilence
and all the land that the sun looks upon
in the east, and he alone will sail over the world.
Alas for you, Babylon! You will serve in triumphs,
though called mistress; Ares comes against Asia,
he comes in truth and will slaughter many of your children.
And then you will send forth your royal man,
named after the number four, furious with the spear,
a formidable archer, along with mighty warriors.
And then indeed between the Cilicians and Assyrians
famine and war will hold sway; but the high-spirited kings
will stir up the terrible strife of soul-devouring conflict.
But you, flee across and leave the king himself;
do not wish to remain, nor be ashamed to be a coward;
for a terrible lion will rush upon you, a raw-flesh-eating beast,
wild, bringing a foreign rule, clad in a mantle upon his shoulders.
Flee the lightning-swift man! An evil yoke will come upon Asia,
and again the whole earth will drink raining slaughter.
But when the Pellaean Ares establishes
the great, wealth-giving city of Egypt, and names it after himself,
[he will meet] fate and death, craftily betrayed by his companions—
for when he has left the Indians and come to Babylon,
a barbarous murder will destroy him around the banquet tables.
Thereafter others will rule over each nation,
people-devouring kings, arrogant and faithless,
for a few years; but a high-spirited, haughty one,
who will strip Europe bare for all like a harvested field,
from the time when all the earth drinks the blood of all tribes,
will depart, having spent the very form of his life.
And there will be other kings, twice four men
from his lineage, all having the same name.
And Egypt will then be a reigning bride,
and the great city of the Macedonian king,
queenly Alexandria, renowned nourisher of cities,
shining with beauty, will alone be the metropolis.
And then let Memphis find fault with the rulers.
And there will be deep peace throughout the whole world;
and the black-soiled earth will then yield more fruits.
And then there will be evil for the Jews, nor will they escape
famine and plague on that unbearable day;
but the black-soiled, fair-eared, newly ordered,
divine land will receive many who perish.
Yet eight kings of marshy Egypt
will complete the number of thirty-three
and two hundred years. But their race
will not all perish, for a female root will sprout forth,
a deadly woman, the betrayer of her own kingdom.
But in their wickedness they will work evil deeds against themselves
thereafter, and one will destroy another;
[a purple-clad father will strike down a warrior father,
and he himself, before he plants another shoot,
will perish at his son's hands; but a root will sprout up thereafter,
growing of itself; from this an offshoot race will arise.]
For there will be a queen of the land by the streams of the Nile,
where it enters the sea through its sevenfold mouths,
and the much-desired name of the twentieth number belongs to her;
she will demand myriad things and gather all wealth
of gold and silver; but treachery will come upon her
from her own men. Then for you again, blessed land,
there will be wars and battles and slaughters of men.
But when many begin to rule over flourishing Rome,
by no means chosen beforehand by the blessed ones, but tyrants,
having become commanders of thousands and of tens of thousands,
and overseers of lawful assemblies, the greatest
Caesars, succeeding one another, will rule all their days;
and the last of these to rule will be of the tenth number,
the last Caesar, stretching out his limbs upon the earth,
struck down in dread war by a hostile man;
whom the sons of Rome, carrying with their own hands,
will bury piously, and heap up a tomb over him,
sharing in remembrance for the sake of his friendship.
But whenever the end of the year’s time arrives,
fulfilling twice two hundred and twice ten years
since your founder, the child of a wild beast, held command,
no longer will a dictator be a ruler of limited term;
but a lord and king will arise, a godlike man.
Know then, O Egypt, that a king is coming against you;
and dread, helmet-flashing Ares will truly come.
And then for you, widow, capture will follow thereafter;
for dread and fierce wars, working evil,
will rage violently around the walls of the land. And in the wars
you yourself, suffering grievous things over the newly wounded,
wretched woman, will flee; but afterward you will come to the bed
of that very terrible one; the marriage will be your final bedfellow.
Alas for you, ill-wed maiden, you will give royal power
to the Roman king, and you will pay in full for all
that you did before in wars and deeds of courage;
you will give the whole land as a dowry to a powerful man,
as far as the interior of Libya and the dark-skinned men.
And you will no longer be a widow, but will live with a lion,
a man-devouring, terrible, and warlike warrior.
And then, wretched woman, you will become unseen among all
mankind, for you will depart with a shameless soul;
and an echoing tomb in its enclosure will receive the revered queen,
alive within, fitted with barrier-gates at the top, skillfully wrought, and a great people will weep for you,
and the king will utter a terrible groan of pity over you.
And then much-toiling Egypt will become a servant,
she who for many years bore trophies against the Indians;
and she will serve shamefully, and mingle tears upon the river,
the fruit-bearing Nile, because although possessing wealth
and abundance of all good things, the nurturer of cities,
she will nourish a race of terrible sheep-devouring men.
Ah, to how many beasts will you become a servant and a prey,
O wealthy Egypt, though giving laws to peoples;
you who formerly exulted even in great kings
will wretchedly serve peoples on account of that people,
whom formerly, when pious, you brought into great misery
of toils and wailings, and placed a plow upon their neck
and watered the fields with human tears.
Therefore the Sovereign himself, the immortal God dwelling in the ether,
will utterly destroy you and send you forth to wailing;
and you will pay for the things you previously did lawlessly,
and at the last you will know that the wrath of God has come upon you.
But as for me, I will go to Pytho and well-towered Panopeus;
there all will declare me to be a true
prophetess by my oracle; yet with a frenzied spirit
someone will say that I am a messenger; but when one approaches my books,
let him not tremble, and all things both future and past
he will know from our verses; then the God-possessed woman
no one will any longer call a frantic chanter of oracles of necessity.
But now, O Sovereign, cause my very lovely voice to cease,
driving away the frenzy and true inspired utterance
and fearful madness, and give a delightful song.
Twelfth Book of the Sibyl
Come now, hear from me of the mournful time of the Latins.
Indeed, first of all, after the perished kings
of Egypt, all of whom the impartial earth carried away,
and after the citizen of Pella, beneath whom all
the East was struck down and the very wealthy West,
whom Babylon exposed, and offered as a corpse to Philip,
falsely declared to be the true son of Zeus or Ammon,
and after him of the race and blood of Assaracus,
who came from Troy, who cleaved the rushing fire,
and after many kings again, after martial men,
and after the infant children of the sheep-devouring beast,
and after six centuries of years have passed
and two decades, while Rome is under a dictator,
there will be a first sovereign from the western sea,
ruling Rome, greatly valiant and a warrior,
who obtained the first of the letters, and having bound you,
he will be established by manslaying Ares, O you of splendid fruits;
you will pay back the outrage which you willingly inflicted;
for he, magnanimous, will excel in wars;
before whom Thrace will cower, and Sicily, and next Memphis,
Memphis cast headlong through the wickedness of leaders
and of an unenslaved woman falling under the spear;
and he will establish laws for peoples and subdue all things.
Having strong glory of the scepter, he will rule for a long time;
for no other sceptered king of the Romans
will ever surpass him by even a short time, not by a single hour,
because God granted everything to him.
[And indeed he showed wondrous, great seasons on the divine earth,
and showed signs for them.
But whenever a star, completely resembling the sun,
shining brightly from heaven, appears in the middle of the day,
even then the hidden Word of the Most High will come,
bearing flesh like unto mortals; but with him
he will increase the power of Rome and the glorious Latins,]
and that great king himself in turn, by his own fate,
will die, having handed over the royal rule to another.
And after him another man, a mighty spearman,
will rule, clad in a purple robe upon his shoulders,
who bears the first stroke of the number three hundred—
he will destroy the Medes and also the arrow-shooting Parthians;
and he himself will overthrow a high-gated city by his own might;
and there will be evil for the city of Egypt and for the Assyrians,
for the Colchians, the Heniochoi, and for those Germans living by the streams of the Rhine along the sandy shores.
He himself will also afterward sack a high-gated city
near the Eridanus, a city scheming evil things.
And then indeed he will fall, struck down by gleaming iron.
And after that another wily man will rule,
who has obtained the number three; and the initial letter
will reveal his name; and he will gather together much gold;
and there will be no satiety of great wealth, but shamelessly
having plundered still more, he will store everything in the earth.
And there will be peace, and Ares will cease from wars.
And he will do much harm, putting greatest trust
in divinations for the sake of his livelihood; but upon him
there will be a very great sign: bloody drops will fall from heaven
when the king is destroyed.
And he will commit many lawless deeds, and will place afflictions
around the neck of the Romans, trusting in divinations;
and he will destroy heads of the senate. And famine will take hold
of the Campanians, Thracians, Macedonians, and Italians;
and Egypt alone will nourish the multitudinous tribes.
And deceiving a virgin maiden with a mystery,
the king himself will destroy her deceitfully; and her the citizens
will bury with sorrow; and having harbored wrath against the ruler,
they all will treacherously mutilate him.
Mighty in flourishing Rome, he will perish at the hands of mighty men.
And again another lord of the number twice ten will rule;
and then wars and mournful sorrows will come upon the Sauromatians,
and upon the Thracians and the javelin-hurling Triballi;
and Roman Ares will destroy them all.
And there will be a fearful sign while he rules
over the land of the Italians and the Pannonians; and around them
there will be a dark night in the middle hour of the day
and a rain of stones from heaven. But thereafter
a mighty ruler and judge of the Italians
shall go into the halls of Hades by his own fate.
Another man shall come in turn, numbering fifty,
terrible and fearful; and he will destroy many
of the best men born to wealth from all cities,
a terrible serpent, the short word of nature. He once will stretch forth
his hands against the leaders, and destroy, and accomplish many things,
competing in games, driving chariots, killing, and daring myriad deeds;
and he shall cut through the mountain of two seas, and stain it with gore.
Yet he shall also vanish, destructive to the Italians,
making himself equal to God, and he will convict a willing people;
and there shall be deep peace while he rules.
[and tremblings of men; and having darted beneath the Ausonians,
strange water yielded from the streams of Ocean;]
Looking around him, he will establish athletic contests for the people,
very many indeed, and he himself will compete in the games
with voice and lyre, singing a song along with the string;
afterward he shall flee again, leaving the royal rule,
and perishing miserably he will pay the penalty for all that he did.
After him three shall rule, two rulers possessing
the number seventy in their names, and one besides these
of the third letter; and one after another shall perish
by mighty Ares, under the hands of an army.
Then a great destroyer of pious men shall come,
a ruler, a man of mighty spirit, a spear-brandishing Ares,
who clearly displays the letter of seventy;
he shall destroy Phoenicia and wipe out Syria;
a sword shall also come upon the Solymian land
as far as the extreme bend of the brine of Tiberias.
Alas, Phoenicia, how much you will endure, deeply mourning!
*With tight routs*, and every nation shall trample you.
Alas, you will go to the Assyrians, and you will see
your infant children enslaved among hostile men
together with your wives and all your livelihood, and your wealth shall perish;
for the deeply mourning wrath of God shall come upon you,
because they did not keep his law, but in all things
served idols with shameful arts.
Many wars again, and battles, and slaughters of men,
famines and plagues, and disturbances of cities.
And at the end of his life, the venerable, great-hearted king,
himself displaying valor, shall fall under the constraint of the army.
Afterward two other men shall rule as kings,
cherishing the memory of their father, the great king,
and exulting greatly among closely-matched warriors.
And one of these shall be a noble man and a ruler,
and he shall have the name of three hundred; but he
shall fall deceitfully, laid low among the armies,
struck down on the soil of Rome by two-edged bronze.
And after him, another man in turn, a mighty spearman,
From the stroke of four he will rule a great kingdom,
whom all mortals throughout the boundless earth will love.
And then indeed there will be a cessation of war throughout all the world.
Yet unto him, from west to east,
all will serve willingly and not by constraint,
and cities will be subject and subservient of their own accord.
For indeed heavenly Sabaoth will bring great renown upon him,
the imperishable God who dwells in the ether.
And then all Pannonia and the Celtic land
famine will diminish and destroy one upon another.
There shall be for the Assyrians, whom the Orontes washes,
buildings and adornment and whatever greater thing is seen anywhere.
And these the great king will cherish and love
above all other citizens; but he himself
will receive a great wound in the midst of his breast,
treacherously seized by a companion at the end of his life;
within the holy, great royal house
he will fall wounded. And after him there will be a ruler,
an august mortal of the number fifty, who beyond all
will destroy many townspeople and citizens of Rome; but he will rule for a short time; for on account of the former king
he will go into the halls of Hades, wounded from behind.
Immediately thereafter another king, a strong spearman,
who has obtained as an engraved beginning the number three hundred,
will rule, and the land of the Thracians, being varied,
